title: The Frolics and forming the Leon Prima band at the Hollywood
summary: He played at the Frolics, then in the Hollywood open-air pavilion band run by Leon Prima and Sharkey. He lists the personnel and writes sketch arrangements.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: It was, uh, a dance band. Again, we had three saxes, three brass, and four rhythm. Uh, this was in the day of the open air dance hall. The first one that I remember was the old Frolics on St. Anne Street, just a few feet away from Broad, North Broad. And that's where I played with, uh, Skiro. He had that job out there. The butcher I mentioned. Joe Skiro. And then, uh, I...
Joe Skiro? I'm confused. The guy from, uh, Dauphine and Iberville?
I'm pretty sure, yes. He had. Clancy, you said before. Clancy, I'm sorry. I said Skiro. We've been to Skiro. That's senile at the cause of these things. Forgive it.
Well, I hate to do that to you. I'm glad you did. I'm leading you. But I didn't want you to

contradict this. No. Well, I usually do anyhow. Okay. But, uh, I played out there, yes. And then, uh, uh, Leon and, uh, Schalker had both worked out there, but not together. They had each worked out there, I should say. And they had decided to go into business, so Hip Kinley, who had run a successful 25 cents club... No, I've got this backwards now. He opened the 25 club later? Let me think about that for a moment. But anyhow, the three of them invested enough money that they took over the Hollywood, and I don't know whether it was reconstructed or what, another big open air pavilion. And they organized the band for that. And the saxophone section was myself, Fazzola, Nina Piconi, uh, Leon Prima, Schalky, and, uh, Julian Lane with the brass section. Augie Chalang was on drums, Louis Macinta was on bass, Frank Pinero was on piano, and, uh, what else do I need? Louis Macinta. Louis Macinta. Fredo Louis Macinta played guitar. That was, that was the size of the band. And I wrote some arrangements for them, sketches more than anything else, uh, to use on the fake tunes, because we did have a full band. But, uh, it was a dance band. You'd play a reading tune, then you might play a fake tune, then once in a while you'd play a waltz, you'd play sets, and there'd be a wrestler if these kids changed partners, and they did a phenomenal business down there.
